RaMP reports FDR 8.6e-19 with 7 of 7 resolved input metabolites hitting the pathway and a fold-enrichment of 875.7; MetaboAnalystR confirms the same KEGG entry with p=5.4e-09 and 6 hits; Mummichog returns it as the top network hit with 16 of 17 pathway members matched (p=0.00160). The 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (C19586) was not resolved by any tool and remains unplaced. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis — converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP reports FDR 8.6e-19 with 7 of 7 resolved input metabolites hitting the pathway and a fold-enrichment of 875.7; MetaboAnalystR confirms the same KEGG entry with p=5.4e-09 and 6 hits; Mummichog returns it as the top network hit with 16 of 17 pathway members matched (p=0.00160). The signal is driven by eight tryptophan-derived metabolites: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), and quinolinic acid (C03722). Three additional sub-pathways appear across paradigms with high significance: Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.1e-08), Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 9.4e-11), and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 9.5e-09), collectively mapping the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid) and the serotonin branch (tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin). Metabolites falling outside tryptophan metabolism — deoxyribose 1-phosphate (pentose phosphate), dihydrolipoate (ascorbate/aldarate), acetylcholine (glycerophospholipid), and N-formyl-L-glutamic acid (folate/alanine metabolism) — appear only in secondary hits with marginal p-values above 0.05 and do not replicate across paradigms. The 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (C19586) was not resolved by any tool and remains unplaced. Structural reconciliation confirmed all 11 resolved metabolites as distinct chemical entities with non-overlapping InChIKey first blocks, eliminating namespace artefacts as an explanation for the enrichment signal.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) with FDR 8.6e-19 and 7 metabolites hit, with the kynurenine branch represented by 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid. Mummichog m/z-direct activity also returns tryptophan metabolism as its top hit (p=0.0029) covering 16 matched features. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA identifies hsa00380 as the sole significant hit (p=5.41e-09) with 6 metabolites. The signal is driven by L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, and quinolinic acid. The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414) captures the kynurenine branch with FDR 9.48e-09. Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) captures the neurotransmitter branch with FDR 2.14e-08. 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 did not appear in any tool result. Deoxyribose 1-phosphate maps to the pentose phosphate pathway via mummichog.

_pathway_peek.pathway_name: Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production

{
  "narrative_text": "Three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis — converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP reports FDR 8.6e-19 with 7 of 7 resolved input metabolites hitting the pathway and a fold-enrichment of 875.7; MetaboAnalystR confirms the same KEGG entry with p=5.4e-09 and 6 hits; Mummichog returns it as the top network hit with 16 of 17 pathway members matched (p=0.00160). The signal is driven by eight tryptophan-derived metabolites: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), and quinolinic acid (C03722). Three additional sub-pathways appear across paradigms with high significance: Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.1e-08), Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 9.4e-11), and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 9.5e-09), collectively mapping the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid) and the serotonin branch (tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin). Metabolites falling outside tryptophan metabolism — deoxyribose 1-phosphate (pentose phosphate), dihydrolipoate (ascorbate/aldarate), acetylcholine (glycerophospholipid), and N-formyl-L-glutamic acid (folate/alanine metabolism) — appear only in secondary hits with marginal p-values above 0.05 and do not replicate across paradigms. The 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (C19586) was not resolved by any tool and remains unplaced. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis — converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP reports FDR 8.6e-19 with 7 of 7 resolved input metabolites hitting the pathway and a fold-enrichment of 875.7; MetaboAnalystR confirms the same KEGG entry with p=5.4e-09 and 6 hits; Mummichog returns it as the top network hit with 16 of 17 pathway members matched (p=0.00160). The signal is driven by eight tryptophan-derived metabolites: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), and quinolinic acid (C03722). Three additional sub-pathways appear across paradigms with high significance: Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.1e-08), Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 9.4e-11), and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 9.5e-09), collectively mapping the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid) and the serotonin branch (tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin). Metabolites falling outside tryptophan metabolism — deoxyribose 1-phosphate (pentose phosphate), dihydrolipoate (ascorbate/aldarate), acetylcholine (glycerophospholipid), and N-formyl-L-glutamic acid (folate/alanine metabolism) — appear only in secondary hits with marginal p-values above 0.05 and do not replicate across paradigms. The 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (C19586) was not resolved by any tool and remains unplaced. Structural reconciliation confirmed all 11 resolved metabolites as distinct chemical entities with non-overlapping InChIKey first blocks, eliminating namespace artefacts as an explanation for the enrichment signal.
